chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him).

Regarding two men who have wealth between them, part of which is in their hands and part is absent from them: they divided the portion in their hands, and each one schemed regarding his share. One of them claimed his share, while the other did not claim. He (the Imam) said: 'Whatever one of them claimed is between them, and whatever is lost is between them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on joint wealth division when one partner claims their share and the other does not?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, transmitted through the chain of his father Imam Ali, addresses the equitable distribution of joint assets where one partner actively claims their share of the liquid assets while the other remains passive. The ruling establishes that the claimed portion remains jointly held rather than fully transferring to the claimant, ensuring that any subsequent loss or depreciation is shared proportionally, reflecting the Shia principle of fairness in partnership dissolution. This mechanism prevents unjust enrichment by the active party and underscores the importance of mutual accountability in financial dealings.
